prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures an egocentric view from a high elevated position—such as a scissor lift around 6–10 metres above a warehouse floor—starting in Frame 1 facing a wall within arm's reach (0.2–0.5 metres) with an electrical junction box, wire mesh cable tray, cables, and the wearer's hands at the bottom-left and top-right corners. As the camera wearer turns downward and to the right across Frames 2 to 5, the wearer's raised left arm and hand appear bright white in the extreme foreground (0.1–0.4 metres away), sweeping across the upper-left and centre in Frames 2–4 and partially occluding the distant warehouse floor below before dropping to the bottom-left edge in Frame 5. On the floor 6–12 metres below, the RGB context reveals a standing person near the bottom-centre looking upward toward the camera wearer, a pallet stack about 3–4 metres to that person's left, and a red-and-white industrial lift/machine and wooden pallets 5–8 metres further ahead near a far doorway, all separated from the adjacent right-hand wall (1–3 metres from the wearer) by a continuous depth gradient. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly isolates the foreground boundary of the raised arm against the similarly toned concrete floor and captures the fine 3D relief of the thin wires and mesh tray in Frame 1. However, the depth map is unreliable for distant floor objects (renderings of the person, pallets, and machinery flatten into uniform dark values in Frames 2–5) and suffers from severe bleeding in Frame 4, where bright foreground values spill from the wearer's arm into the background wall and floor.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map is completely blank across Frames 1 to 3, failing to segment the wall-mounted electrical box, cable tray, and hands within 0.5 metres in Frame 1, as well as the wearer's raised foreground arm (0.1–0.4 metres away) and the warehouse scene 6–12 metres below in Frames 2 and 3. In Frame 4, it detects a single 'person' mask (pink) representing the camera wearer's raised arm and hand spanning the centre and right foreground within arm's reach (0.1–0.3 metres), which heavily occludes the background wall and floor as the arm lowers. In Frame 5, after the wearer's arm drops almost entirely out of view save for two fingers at the bottom-left, the map detects a single 'truck' mask (olive green) in the middle-upper ground roughly 8–10 metres below and ahead, corresponding to the red-and-white industrial machine positioned 4–5 metres behind the standing person on the floor and 3 metres right of the stacked pallets. While the Frame 5 'truck' mask helps isolate the footprint of that piece of floor machinery from the adjacent wooden pallets and open doorway in the cluttered RGB view, the map is largely unreliable across the sequence. It completely misses the standing person on the floor (who faces and looks upward toward the camera wearer from 6–8 metres below in Frames 2–5), misses the wearer's arm in Frames 1–3, and produces a noisy, jagged boundary on the 'person' mask in Frame 4 that bleeds into the background.
descriptions.pose: The body and hand skeleton map is completely black across all 5 frames, detecting neither yellow body keypoints nor magenta hand keypoints anywhere in the sequence. From the RGB context, the camera wearer's hands are within 0.2–0.5 metres manipulating cables at the top-right and bottom-left of Frame 1, and the wearer's raised left arm sweeps across the foreground (0.1–0.4 metres away) from Frame 2 to Frame 4 before dropping to leave only a pointing hand at the bottom-left of Frame 5, occluding large portions of the warehouse floor in Frames 2–4. Meanwhile, in Frames 2 through 5, a second person stands on the warehouse floor roughly 6–8 metres below and slightly to the left of the right-hand wall, positioned 3–4 metres from a stack of blue boxes to their left and 4–5 metres in front of the red-and-white machinery, with their body and head angled upward toward the camera wearer and nothing within their immediate arm's reach. Because the pose estimator fails completely, it provides no spatial information beyond what is visible in the RGB strip and cannot help resolve the exact articulation of the distant person's upturned posture or the wearer's close-up finger positions. The map is entirely unreliable here due to extreme egocentric self-occlusion and proximity of the wearer's limbs at the frame boundaries, combined with the steep overhead viewing angle and small pixel scale of the person standing far below.
